question: do the sibling Lax artifacts agree where their definitions coincide, and is the 'probe artifact not reproducible' item real?

canonical_metrics.whole_field_L1: relative L1, whole field (Gauss-node Legendre weighting)
canonical_metrics.whole_field_L2: relative L2, whole field (Gauss-node Legendre weighting)
canonical_metrics.band_L1: relative L1, analytic region only (wave band removed)

lax_case_pool.note: the ledger artifact; 9-leg ladder N=100/200/400 x p=1/2/3

dt_semantics_declared: dt_last = time-truncated final step; dt_mean = final_time/steps
lax_asymptotic_probe.note: p3 order attribution; extends the ladder to N=800

lax_resolution_requirement.note: what resolution the 3 % bar needs (p3.N400 -> p3.N800)

lax_certified_configuration.note: cheapest (p, N) that certifies the 3 % bar (DOF-ordered)

dt_semantics_declared: dt = final_time/steps (mean step); a time-truncated final step, when recorded, is kept under dt_last*
lax_case_pool_limiter_arms.note: single-knob limiter attribution; dt repaired in place (no re-run)

checks.C1: the meaning of the bare key `dt` is resolved for every publisher: either declared by a dt_semantics string, or verified by C2 to be final_time/steps (so no reader has to guess and no file is rewritten only to carry a label)
checks.C3: 0 < dt_last <= dt_mean (1 + 1e-12) wherever dt_last is recorded
checks.C4: the bare key `dt` maps to the same canonical quantity in every publisher
checks.C5: legs shared by >= 2 publishers agree on every commonly published canonical metric to <= 1e-12 relative
checks.C6: a fresh solve of a shared leg reproduces the committed canonical metrics to <= 1e-12 relative (evaluated by the reconciliation driver)

cross_metric_diagnostic.note: differences a reader sees when comparing two *different* error definitions on the same leg; not drift

payload_live.floor_reason: post-hoc cross-platform reproducibility floor: bitwise (1e-12) equality is not achievable between the loong64 artifacts and this x86 host; the floor is 80x the measured worst (1.25e-05), three orders below the 3 % case tolerance and one order below the ~1e-4 discrepancy the residual-gap doc reported
payload_live.note: current code, same measurement path as benchmarks.lax_case_pool (Gauss-node Legendre weighting, exact Riemann denominator); the legs were measured one per process because a single-process run exceeds the local short-test budget -- each row is one fresh solve of the current code against the committed artifact

cross_definition_gap.note: same leg, *different* definition: the size of the discrepancy a reader gets by comparing mismatched keys

quoted_dt.conclusion: the 12 % 'dt difference' is dt_last vs dt_mean of one run; not solver drift

figures.caption: Recorded step sizes per leg: circles = dt_mean (final_time/steps), crosses = dt_last; hollow red = the value the bare `dt` key carried in the limiter-arms artifact before the repair. The legacy key sat on the dt_last lane, which is what made a 12-94 % 'difference' look like drift when compared against dt_mean.

Left: whole-field L1 (filled) against band-limited L1 (hollow) on identical legs -- differences of the same order as the 'discrepancy' the residual-gap doc reports. Right: the same artifacts compared only where the definitions coincide; every pair is at or below the 1e-12 contract tolerance.
